topicCandidates: A duty-first comparison of Artist, Entertainer, Journalist, Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Cultural Activities, and Business Manager for creative and media work.
Artist as income-producing artistic activity outside Entertainer, including contracted and independent work, expected income, career evidence, recognition, and portfolio evidence.
Entertainer activity categories beyond performers, including advertising, broadcast or film production, commercial photography, and commercial audio or video recording.
Journalist activity under contract with a foreign news organization, including dispatched, locally employed, and qualifying freelance relationships.

Legal/Accounting Services as a qualification-controlled status for the professions expressly identified in the landing criteria, not a general route for legal, compliance, bookkeeping, or finance jobs.
Medical Services as licensed medical practice, including every profession named in the current criteria, remuneration parity, institution conditions, and the special assistant-nurse limitation.

Nursing Care as work or instruction under a Japanese organization contract by a registered Certified Care Worker, separated from Medical Services, Specified Skilled Worker, and EPA Designated Activities routes.

Religious Activities as religious work by personnel dispatched by a foreign religious organization, with the dispatching and receiving bodies, religious standing, remuneration, and incidental duties made explicit.
Skilled Labor as a closed set of specialized industrial skill categories with category-specific experience or achievement criteria, rather than a synonym for any experienced worker.
Available periods, extension evidence, organization changes, multiple contracts, outside activity, and transitions for all eight statuses.
Receiving-organization duties and evidence for employers, hospitals, care facilities, production organizations, news organizations, religious organizations, and regulated professional practices.
userSituations: A graphic designer, illustrator, photographer, filmmaker, or content creator trying to choose a status from an English job title rather than the actual activity, income model, client, and organization.
An independent artist relying on commissions, royalties, exhibitions, or several contracts who needs to show a concrete activity plan, expected income, and professional record.
A commercial photographer or film worker who assumes Artist applies even though Entertainer materials expressly cover some commercial production activities.
A freelance correspondent who has a contract with a foreign news organization but is not a conventional employee.

A paralegal, compliance analyst, bookkeeper, financial analyst, or consultant who sees legal or accounting in a title but does not perform a profession reserved to one of the listed qualified practitioners.
A foreign-trained doctor, nurse, therapist, or other health professional who has not yet obtained the Japanese qualification required for the proposed licensed work.
A person searching for nurse or caregiver work who needs to distinguish Medical Services, Nursing Care, Specified Skilled Worker nursing care, and an EPA candidate route.
A care-work student who passed the national examination but is waiting for Certified Care Worker registration and may need the temporary Designated Activities bridge.
A religious worker invited by a Japanese congregation without a clear dispatch relationship from a foreign religious organization.
A foreign-cuisine cook, sports coach, pilot, craftsperson, trainer, or sommelier who needs the exact Skilled Labor category and its specific experience or achievement evidence.
An experienced general tradesperson who assumes Skilled Labor means any skilled occupation, or confuses it with Specified Skilled Worker.
A receiving organization preparing a COE application and needing to understand what evidence it can supply without promising an immigration outcome.
edgeCasesAndExceptions: Artist excludes activities assigned to Entertainer; artistic quality or a portfolio alone does not decide that boundary.

Entertainer includes more than on-stage performers. Current official materials separate several activity and venue categories and include advertising, broadcast or film production, commercial photography, and commercial recording.

Journalist requires a foreign-news-organization contract, but that contract can be an employment, dispatch, or qualifying non-employment relationship; freelancer does not automatically mean ineligible.
Photojournalist, commercial photographer, fine-art photographer, and an in-house studio photographer can raise different route questions despite sharing the word photographer.
Cultural Activities covers unpaid artistic activity or specialized study and must not be presented as a paid creative-work route.
Owning a creative business does not automatically convert production work into Business Manager activity, and being called a creative director does not establish genuine management.
Legal/Accounting Services is limited to the named Japanese-law qualification categories. A foreign degree, overseas license, or related corporate title alone does not establish eligibility.
Unregulated legal support, compliance, finance, accounting support, and consulting may require comparison with Engineer/Specialist or Business Manager according to the real duties.
Medical Services requires the applicable Japanese qualification. Current criteria name fourteen professions and require remuneration at least equivalent to a Japanese worker performing the work.
Assistant nurses have a distinct current criterion limiting the work to training within four years after obtaining the Japanese license; this must not be generalized to registered nurses.
For pharmacists and several allied-health professions, the current criteria also require invitation by a Japanese medical institution or pharmacy.
Medical research, hospital administration, medical translation, and health-technology work do not become Medical Services merely because the workplace is a hospital.
Nursing Care requires Certified Care Worker registration and a Japanese organization contract; the route has applied regardless of qualification-acquisition pathway since April 1, 2020.

A nursing-care facility can employ people under different programs, so workplace and job title do not identify Nursing Care, Specified Skilled Worker, Technical Intern Training or Employment for Skill Development, or EPA Designated Activities.

Religious Activities depends on dispatch by a foreign religious organization and religious work. Ordinary teaching, charity administration, commercial work, or a domestic job offer must not be treated as qualifying merely because a religious organization is involved.
Incidental language teaching is contemplated in the Religious Activities application form, but unrelated paid work still requires a separate activity analysis.
Skilled Labor is category-bound. Extensive experience in an occupation outside the listed criteria does not make the status available.
Foreign-cuisine preparation generally uses a ten-year experience rule including relevant foreign education, while qualifying Thai cuisine cooks have a treaty-based five-year evidence route.
Foreign-specific architecture can use ten years of experience, or five years when working under a person with at least ten years of the relevant experience.

Pilots, sports instructors, and sommeliers use distinct evidence: at least 250 flight hours for the relevant pilot route; experience or international-competition criteria for sports instruction; and experience plus competition, representation, or designated-certification evidence for sommeliers.

Skilled Labor and Specified Skilled Worker are different statuses with different eligible sectors, tests or experience rules, support systems, family rules, and periods; similar work words must not collapse them.
All statuses in this batch currently list five, three, or one year, or three months, except Entertainer, which lists three years, one year, six months, three months, or thirty days.
An available period is not a promise of the period granted, and renewal depends on the continuing facts, records, compliance, and qualifying activity.
jurisdictionVariables: National immigration statutes, landing criteria, ministerial notices, current ISA application pages, and effective-dated checklists.
The governing Japanese professional-qualification and registration law for legal, accounting, medical, and care work.
The real activity, contract structure, remuneration, work location, receiving organization, and principal-versus-incidental duties.
Profession-specific regulators, licensing bodies, and institution permissions; immigration permission does not replace professional licensing.
Treaty-based criteria such as the Thailand-Japan route for qualifying Thai cuisine cooks.
EPA country and candidate-program rules for nurses and care workers, which are separate from the ordinary Medical Services and Nursing Care statuses.
Regional ISA examination and requests for additional evidence; local practice must not be described as changing the national status definition.

supports: Temporary Designated Activities bridge after the care-worker examination

contentImpacts.reason: Give designers, artists, photographers, filmmakers, journalists, performers, and independent creators a central activity-first comparison without making a title an eligibility result.
Separate licensed medical practice, Certified Care Worker employment, Specified Skilled Worker nursing care, EPA candidates, research, administration, and qualification-transition situations.
Add the distinct activity tests, contract models, evidence, periods, renewal, transitions, and creative-profession comparisons.
Name every covered profession, explain the Japanese qualification boundary, and distinguish adjacent corporate legal, compliance, finance, and consulting work.
Name every covered medical profession, explain Japanese licensing and special conditions, and separate care-worker and program routes.
Explain foreign-organization dispatch, religious standing, receiving-organization evidence, incidental work, periods, renewal, and transitions.
Present the complete category map and category-specific experience, achievement, treaty, employer, and evidence rules, with a clear Specified Skilled Worker comparison.
Add source-backed structured records for the eight statuses without treating search aliases as legal classifications.
Connect Engineer/Specialist, Cultural Activities, Business Manager, Researcher, Specified Skilled Worker, Designated Activities, outside-activity, employer, and work-change guidance.
Index ordinary-language professions, common questions, Japanese terms, and comparison routes while stating the missing facts needed for a reliable answer.

scopeBoundaries: Do not present an occupation title, portfolio, overseas license, employer label, or years of experience as an eligibility decision.
Do not reproduce every application checklist item in prose; link the current official checklist and explain the evidence categories and important exceptions.
Do not provide individualized legal, licensing, tax, labor, or professional-practice advice.
Do not merge Medical Services, Nursing Care, Specified Skilled Worker, EPA Designated Activities, or medical-study routes.
Do not merge Skilled Labor with Specified Skilled Worker or general skilled employment.
Do not split every creative occupation into a standalone article until the central comparison guide shows a demonstrated navigation need.
Keep all materially rewritten guidance at needs-review until explicit human editorial approval.
unresolvedQuestions: Approve the proposed medical-and-care comparison guide as the second new comparison article in Iteration 6.

Keep Skilled Labor versus Specified Skilled Worker as a prominent comparison within the two existing status guides rather than create another standalone article unless implementation proves too dense.
Use only current primary criteria for profession-specific limits in Medical Services; do not preserve historical restrictions unless a current source or a clearly labeled history note requires them.
During implementation, decide whether film-production or independent-creator material needs a later focused guide after the approved creative-and-media comparison is drafted.
priorApprovals: The central creative-and-media comparison, searchable role inventory, and deeper Artist, Entertainer, and Journalist treatment were approved on 2026-09-11 in the creative-and-media discovery amendment.

scopeApproval.note: The editor approved the proposed Iteration 6 scope, including the medical-and-care comparison guide and the recommendation to keep Skilled Labor versus Specified Skilled Worker within existing guides unless implementation becomes too dense.
